article.name: Flowix
article.summary: Flowix is an agent-workspace application whose local MCP/CLI interface lets agents search and manage Markdown notes and structured collections inside configured notebooks. Markdown files are canonical note content, with a rebuildable SQLite projection for indexed access.

contact.note: The official README at the reviewed commit and official project website were checked for a published contact email; neither listed one. No address was inferred from commit or profile metadata or third-party directories.

who_what.text: The public project is maintained under the Text2Future GitHub organization. It is an open-source desktop/workspace application with a local CLI and an MCP bundle. The bundle starts flowix-cli over stdio and reads the configured local notebook data; its documentation describes memo search/read/create/edit and collection access, not a remote Flowix memory service.

architecture.text: Notebook registry metadata is stored in a device-local SQLite database at the Flowix config directory's db/local.db. Each notebook is a separately configured directory. Markdown files are canonical note content; the per-notebook SQLite note index is a rebuildable projection and does not supply note bytes. The projection stores note path and metadata including title, preview, timestamps, tags, todos, and agent labels.

The MCP bundle exposes a structured memo tool with note discovery, list/tags/show/search, create/edit/write/delete, collection list/describe/query/read and mutation, and artifact actions. Collections expose typed fields and records across note, media, and work-document domains. This workspace data model does not impose a fact ontology or claim-level evidence schema.

behavior.text: Write: note creation writes Markdown in a selected notebook and optional folder, defaulting the title to Untitled. Addresses can be notebook-relative or explicitly notebook-qualified. The resolver rejects empty, absolute, dot, and parent-traversal paths and checks that the notebook directory is available. Collection actions separately support typed collection creation and record or note additions.

Update and correction: edit replaces exact nonempty text only when it occurs exactly once. Full-note write checks an optional SHA-256 body version and saves against the current body; a concurrent change returns a conflict rather than silently overwriting it. MCP requires expectedVersion for write and delete. The inspected note interface does not establish a fact-level correction history or current-value adjudication.

Delete: the addressed note is version-checked and passed to the core checked-delete operation. This is file deletion; the inspected path does not establish erasure from backups, external copies, or synchronized replicas. Collection deletion behavior was outside this note-operation inspection.

Retrieval: search accepts query text and optional notebook and tag filters. Without a notebook filter it selects all available configured notebooks, reconciles each note index, and returns matching titles, snippets, paths, and notebook-qualified addresses; show returns the Markdown body. List/search paging uses offsets and a snapshot token to detect changed results. Source inspection does not measure retrieval quality.

Scope: notebooks organize note directories and explicit addresses bind operations to a notebook. Search can be narrowed to one notebook, but the default search spans all available notebooks. The MCP source states that MCP access is not a filesystem sandbox and hosts must restrict other entry points separately. No user/project authorization guarantee or cross-scope leakage result was established.

Provenance and evidence: the note projection exposes timestamps, tags, todos, and agent labels, while Markdown remains the content source. The inspected note schema and MCP operations do not require claim-level citations, source passages, confidence, review state, or correction history. User-authored notes may contain those details, but retrieved assertions are not guaranteed to carry supporting evidence.

Efficiency and observability: canonical Markdown plus a rebuildable per-notebook SQLite projection supports indexed access; searches reconcile the projection first. The MCP surface provides bounded results, snapshot-aware paging, and process-local request-ID deduplication for collection additions. These are implementation observations only; the inspected paths do not establish latency, storage overhead, token/cost accounting, or memory-quality telemetry.

metrics.evidence: No answerable retrieval workload or adjudication was run.
No unanswerable-query workload or abstention calibration was measured.
Version-checked note edits are visible in source, but no post-correction current-value or stale-result probes were run.
The note delete path was inspected, but no post-delete leakage probes or replica/backup audit were run.
Notebook filters exist; no forbidden cross-notebook, cross-user, or cross-project probes were run.

metrics.domain: Evidence support precision and citation coverage
metrics.evidence: The inspected interface does not require claim-level evidence; no response-claim adjudication workload was run.
No operation latency distribution was collected.
No acknowledged-write to first-correct-recall timing was collected.
No provider charges or price schedule were measured.
Markdown and SQLite storage boundaries were inspected, but no corpus-attributable storage size was measured.
Markdown-backed notes, rebuildable SQLite indexing, reconciliation, snapshot paging, and process-local collection deduplication are implementation observations, not quantified results.

limits.text: This is a bounded, read-only inspection of official documentation, the memory bundle and schema, path-based note operations, notebook registry, and note index at the verified repository head. Flowix, its tests, and benchmarks were not run.

The review cannot establish end-to-end retrieval correctness, calibrated abstention, correction accuracy, physical erasure across copies, authorization isolation, latency, cost, storage efficiency, or production behavior. Atlas descriptions and assessment are not used as evidence.

benchmark.text: Benchmark status is not_run. No Flowix runtime, tests, or benchmark workload was run. Project metric definitions, fixture, and execution-status record are protocol/status references, not Flowix results.
